newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- softer after supply, data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- softer after supply, data.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were mostly flat with a softer tone early Thursday, reacting to increased supply and negative economic data reports, market participants said.
"It's a tad weaker again," one trader said. "It seems like there hasn't been a lot of good news since last week."
The Labor Department said initial state jobless claims fell to 332,000 in the week ended June 21, from a revised 346,000 the prior week.
After the data, the 30-year Treasury bond was down 7/32 at 98-10/32 to yield 6.76 percent.
A second municipal trader attributed the weaker secondary to the large calendar of new deals.
Early new issue pricings Thursday included a $346 million Philadelphia Airport bond deal, which Lehman Brothers tentatively priced at a top yield of 5.80 percent in 2018.
Lehman also tentatively priced a $65 million Sarasota County, Fla., hospital deal. The bonds came at a top yield of 5.60 percent in 2020.
Thursday's calendar is expected to total $922 million in 26 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $785 million in 11 sales, with Philadelphia's issue topping the list.
On the competitive side, 15 sales totaling $137 million are scheduled. A $32 million Virginia Housing Development Authority deal at 1100 EDT is the largest.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract lost 8/32 at 116-30/32. The September T-bond contract lost 7/32 at 111-16/32. The MOB narrowed to 174 ticks from 175 at the close on Wednesday.

Actively traded secondary bonds included Delaware River Port Authority FGIC 5-1/2s of 2026. Bids were down 3/8 from Wednesday at 98-7/8. Jefferson County, Ala., FGIC 5-3/4s of 2027 were up 1/4 at 100-1/4.
